payload.name: Verify existing-memory match before duplicate SKIP
payload.description: When deciding to SKIP a candidate during CRUD because information is already represented, first confirm the matching memory actually exists in the retrieved pool.
content: During CRUD, before applying SKIP with the reason 'information already represented', require an actual matching memory in the retrieved existing-memory pool; if no relevant memory is present, the candidate is new and should be ADDed or MERGEd instead.
Do not assume a fact is already represented merely because earlier messages discussed a similar topic; absence of a retrieved memory makes the SKIP justification invalid.

solves: During construction CRUD, a valid new fact candidate is sometimes skipped with the justification that the information is already represented even though no matching memory exists in the retrieved pool, causing a true fact to be lost. This rule applies whenever a SKIP decision is considered and requires grounding any 'already represented' claim in an explicit existing-memory match before skipping.
